Commentary.Commentary: The hosts' bowlers were on the money from the word go. Especially, Shannon Gabriel who was in his elements. He picked up a 5-wicket haul and broke the backbone of the opposition. Kemar Roach was very effective as well and finished with a 4-fer. The home side conceded too many for their liking at the fag end but they will back themselves to put up a resolute show with the bat. Will they be able to do so or will the Sri Lankans come good on a helpful pitch? Stay with us for the Windies' reply with the bat.

However, the tourists kept on losing wickets on a consistent basis. Amidst all this, Dinesh Chandimal stayed tall and played an innings of substance. After being given a reprieve on 14 by Devon Smith, he ensured that he makes the opportunity count. Against a fiery bowling line up, he batted with grit and determination. He found handy support from the No. 10 batsman, Rajitha which helped him to reach a well-deserved ton.

A brilliant knock from the Sri Lankan skipper has given the visitors some sort of a fighting total on a difficult surface. He has shown that if you have the mental toughness, you can score runs no matter what the circumstances are. After winning the toss and opting to bat, things didn't go according to the script for the away side. Two wickets fell cheaply for them and then started the re-building phase. Two useful stands, 44 and 67 to be precise, gave the tourists something to work upon.

OUT! Roach doesn't make the hosts rue the no ball as he gets the wicket of Kumara. Serves a full ball outside off. The batsman flashes hard but gets a thickish outside edge and the ball flies to gully. An alert Shai Hope positioned there dives forward and completes a very good catch to wrap things up. SRI LANKA HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 253!
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

Oh my my! What just happened? Chandimal was running back to the pavilion but he has been called back by the umpire, courtesy the no ball from Roach. It is a touch short and on the leg side, Chandimal closes his bat face a bit too early and the ball goes off the leading edge towards point. Bishoo stationed there sets himself under the ball and grabs the catch. The Windies rejoice the wicket but hang on says the umpire and goes upstairs to check the no ball. And much to the bowler's surprise, he has overstepped by quite some margin. The support staff don't look too pleased.
Some extra bounce of the length ball and thuds into Chandimal's thigh pads.
The batsman does well to leave that bouncer alone.

SIX! Bang! Right out of the screws from the Sri Lankan skipper. He has changed gears it seems. Gets a full ball around off and he picks it up and hits it over the mid off fielder. It has enough on it go over the boundary. These are handy runs for the visitors.
Short of a length around off and punched off the back foot by Chandimal through covers. Two runs taken before the fielder in the deep comes around to cut it off.
Short and down the leg side and Kumara leaves it for the keeper.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground for nothing.
Full and into the stumps, Chandimal presents the full face and guides it to mid on for a single.
Back of a length, jagging into the batsman, who does well to defend it.
Now off the front foot through covers. Gets a fullish length delivery on off and goes with hard hands once again. The ball goes through the covers and two more runs added to the total.

FOUR! Dinesh Chandimal has to play a few shots now and he gets into action straightaway. Banged in short, angling into him. He goes hard with the pull and plays it in front of mid-wicket to start the over with a boundary.
Attempted poke at the ball from the crease but misses it.
Roach goes around the wicket and serves it wide outside off. Left alone by the new batsman.
Lahiru Kumara is the last man in.

OUT! Roach has his third and Sri Lanka lose their ninth. Full, swinging away and wide of off stump, entices Rajitha to go for an ambitious shot. He goes for a booming drive but only manages a faint outside edge and the keeper does the rest.
Blocks the good length delivery with the full face of the face.
Play and a miss. That channel of uncertainty outside off is proving difficult.
Delivers it from wide of the crease, on a good length and around off stump. Rajitha manages to defend it off the inside half.
Kemar Roach is back into the attack.
Good length ball well outside off, left alone.
Full ball outside off, eased to sweeper cover for a single.
Back of a length ball outside off, kept out towards point.
Short ball angling across Dinesh. He sways away from the line of the delivery.

FOUR! 11th Test hundred for Dinesh Chandimal, his third as the Test skipper of Sri Lanka! It has been a top, top knock from him on a testing surface. Considering the circumstances he came in, it was not an easy task. Though he was dropped early on in the innings as well, it is the character which matters and he proved every bit of it. Coming to the delivery, it is on a length in the avenue of apprehension. He gets squared up and gets an outside edge that goes past the slip cordon and through to the third man fence. He has a big smile on his face and looks up to the heavens. Punches the air in delight and gets a hug from his partner. Well played, captain! Leading from the front.
No nervousness for Chandimal on 99. He is cool as a cucumber. On a length outside off, the skipper leans ahead and let it be.
This one is well outside off, Rajitha has nothing to do with it.
Outside off, Kasun drives it with the spin through covers and collects a brace.
Tossed up in the same zone, pushed off the front foot towards mid off.
Floated on off, Rajitha lunges forward in defense.
Chandimal moves onto 99. He leans ahead and knocks this one down towards long off to rotate strike.
Tossed up on a fullish length outside off, Chandimal goes forward and defends it right under his eyes.

Not Out! The hosts lose both their reviews. Well, there is no bat involved but there is glove involved. However, the batsman won't be dismissed. I will give you the explanation why. Shortish delivery angling in from outside off and climbing on Rajitha. He gets into a tangle as he tries to fend it off as the ball goes off something towards the second slip fielder. He catches it and goes up in an appeal. His teammates join him as well. Well, the umpire moves away with a smile on his face. Holder consults with his teammates and challenges the decision. The replays roll in. The Snicko shows a spike as the ball goes past the gloves. The third umpire mentions that while the ball deflected off the glove of the back arm, Rajitha's hand had come off the handle. In such a case, a batsman can't be adjudged out. Hence, he survives.
The hosts feel that they have their man and go upstairs regarding a catch appeal. Kasun Rajitha is the man in question. However, it seems that there was no bat involved.
Shows the full face of the bat and blocks it down off the back foot.
Unusual bounce from Cummins but down the leg side. Dowrich does well to dive to his left and stops it from going for a boundary.
On a fullish length outside off, punched off the back foot through covers and they take a single amidst some confusion.
Played to the point region by the batsman for nothing.

Safe! Full outside off and Chandimal flashes hard at the delivery. The ball goes off the outside edge and wide of the gully fielder. The fielder at third man runs in and throws the ball quickly back to the keeper. Chandimal wants two straightaway and calls his partner through. The throw comes in at the striker's end as Chandimal tries to get in with a dive. Dowrich takes the bails off and appeals. The umpire takes it upstairs but the replays show that the Sri Lankan skipper is safe.
Another solid defense off the front foot to end the over.
Flights this one around off and Rajitha is happy to defend it off the front foot.
Works it to mid on and takes a single.
Tossed up on off and defended with a straight bat by the skipper.
Floated this one on the stumps and blocked off the front foot by the batsman.
Flatter one around off and blocked off the back foot by Chandimal.

Lands it on a good length, around off and Chandimal gets an inside edge on his pads. The ball drops beside the pitch and the batsmen scamper for a run. The bowler puts in the yards, dives and throws towards the stumps but misses as Rajitha desperately tries to make his crease. A direct hit would have made things interesting.
Full, around off, the batsman gets behind the line and plays it through covers. Two runs added to the total.
Punched to mid-wicket for nothing.
On a good length and on to the hips of Chandimal who tries to tickle it fine but misses. The ball thuds into his thigh pad.
Similar length and blocked off the front foot.
On a back of a length and extracting some extra bounce. Chandimal blocks it with one hand coming off the blade.
Shorter in length, kept out watchfully.
Fuller in length, played with soft hands towards mid on.
Tossed up ball, defended solidly off the front foot.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.

Not Out! Chandimal was the main man and hence the review. As expected, it has been wasted. Floated around off, spinning away. Chandimal again goes for the reverse sweep but misses to get hit on the pads. An appeal ensues but umpire Ian Gould shakes his head. Bishoo has a chat with his skipper and they decide to go for the review. Time for the replays. The impact is outside off and it is also spinning past the off stump.
A decision for an LBW goes upstairs. Chandimal is the man in question. Seems that it will miss the off stump.

FOUR! Innovative! Chandimal has thought out of the box and has received the result. Shorter in length outside off, allows the skipper to line it up. He goes for the fancy reverse sweep and connects well. Gets it through third man and moves into the nineties with that boundary.
On a length outside off, Kasun plays at it but misses.

Close shave! Angling in sharply from a good length to go past Rajitha's defense and ping him on the thigh pads. The ball lobs over to the short leg fielder who takes it. The Windies appeal but the umpire stays put. Replays confirm there was no bat involved.
Bouncer but it is outside off not making the tailender play. He sits underneath it.
Short of a length ball in line of the stumps, Dinesh gets inside the line of it and tucks it towards fine leg to rotate strike.
Cummins hits the deck hard but the ball is way outside off. Dinesh slaps it over covers and collects a couple of runs.
Short but it is not well-directed. Down the leg side and Chandimal ducks under it with ease.
Miguel Cummins returns for a bowl.
Short this time and stays low. Rajitha has ample time to block it.
Tossed up nicely outside off, played with the spin towars covers.
Dinesh is nimble on his feet and drives it past the diving Bishoo for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Slow through the air, Chandimal skips down the track and pushes it back to the bowler.
Shortish delivery, cut away off the back foot towards backward point.
Drinks time. Meanwhile, Bishoo is back.
The batsman shoulders arms to the wide delivery to let that one through.

OOH! That came in sharply. On a short of a length and coming into the tailender. He looks to defend but the angle and bounce makes it difficult for him. In the end, the ball hits high on his bat and he somehow manages to keep it down.
Short and wide and left alone by Rajitha.
Yorker this time. The batsman does well to dig it out.
On a probing short of a length, outside off and Rajitha goes for the shot but misses.
Full and outside off, the batsman gets a bottom edge! The keeper gathers it on the bounce.
FOUR! WOW! Timing and authority oozing from that shot. Chandimal reads the short ball early and pulls it to the square leg boundary. Lone warrior for Sri Lanka, battling it out in the middle.
Drives the full delivery straight to mid off.
Short delivery on his hips and tucked away to square leg for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Stays low and goes past the bat of Rajitha.
Short and wide of off, the batsman punches it hard but straight to the sweeper cover fielder. One run added to the total.
Blocks the back of a length delivery off the back foot.
The ball is way wide on the leg side but the batsman still goes after it and misses.
Kasun Rajitha comes out to bat.

OUT! Yes, that is dead and the visitors lose a review! The Sri Lankan tail is in no mood to hang around with their skipper. They are falling like nine pins. Kudos to Gabriel for making their life hard and getting a fifer, his third in Test cricket. Coming to the delivery, it is full and darting in from wide of the crease. The ball skids off the surface and hits Lakmal's pads in front of the sticks. The umpire has no hesitation in raising his finger. The batsman looks at his skipper and after a little chat, goes for the review. The Hawk Eye shows that the ball would have crashed into the middle and leg stump. Chandimal needs to take charge of the situation else he might not have partners to play with.
Review time! Lakmal has been adjudged LBW but he has a look at his skipper and decides to challenge the decision. Seems dead to the naked eye though.
Touch fuller this time and Lakmal is late on it as he fails to make contact.

FOUR! OOH! Lucky, very lucky! Gabriel almost had his fifth scalp. Bowls it on a back of a length and the natural angle brings it in. As usual, some extra bounce and a wild hoick across the line from Lakmal. He gets a thick outside edge and the ball flies over the jumping keeper. A boundary results.
Full, around off, Lakmal blocks it off the front foot.
Dot ball to end the over. On a back of a length, angling into the skipper who presents the full face of the bat and blocks it.
The point fielder comes in now. The other fielders inside the ring also take a few steps forward, all looking to save the single.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
NO BALL! First one of the innings courtesy Kemar Roach! He overstepped there by some margin. On a short of a length outside and left alone by Chandimal.
Short and wide again and nicely punched off the back foot through the cover region. The fielder runs after it but can't stop the batsmen from taking two. 200 up for Sri Lanka.

Chandimal has taken a blow on his right hand. There have been numerous occasions when the ball has taken off from the good length area and has caused concerns for the batsmen. Out comes the physio and applies the magic spray.

Nicely done by the skipper! Short and rising into the grille of the batsman, who does well to keep it down from such height. The ball goes in the air but drops well in front of the third slip fielder. He looks in some pain.
Punches the short of a length delivery through covers and changes strike.
Short and wide and Chandimal cuts it behind to the deep backward point fielder. One run added to the total.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and presents the full face of the bat to block it.
Punches the short of a length delivery to covers and takes a single.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Too straight from Gabriel and the angle takes it down the leg side.
FOUR! Short and wide and Lakmal's eyes lit up. He goes hard at the ball and gets a thick outside edge. The ball flies between the gully fielder and slip cordon and Lakmal gets off the mark as well.
Lands it on a good length and Chandimal clips it down the leg side for a single.
Suranga Lakmal is the next man in.

OUT! And... Gone! The left-handers are having a nightmare against this fast Windies bowling line up. Keeps it on a back of a length, around off and forces Dananjaya to fend at it, who does exactly that. The bat hangs in the air, the ball kisses the outside edge and Dowrich takes a nice low catch in front of his eyes.
Consistency from Roach. Keeping it outside off on a short length and making the batsman have a go at it. Too good for Dananjaya to make any contact.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
On a fuller length outside off and punched through cover-point for two. It was a bit uppish but safe.
No foot movement and wild swing from the crease. Fortunately for him, it misses his willow.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Kemar Roach returns for a bowl.
Back of a length and darted into his body, Chandimal sways away from the line and lets it pass down the leg side.
Drives the fullish delivery off the front foot but straight to the cover fielder.
Lets the ball through to the keeper.
Similar delivery from the bowler and tucked away to square leg for another two.

Touch straight on a length and worked away through the mid-wicket region. It could have been a tight second run had Cummins collected it cleanly but not to be. Chandimal gets away with the second run.

Is that from the bat? Probably not. Keeps it on a good length and darts in with the angle. The batsman misses the line as the ball thuds into his pads. The ball goes in the air and the fielder at gully dives to his front and claims a catch. Appeal from behind the wicket and the bowler but the umpire doesn't seem interested.
Dananjaya shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Another swing and a miss outside the off stump.
Touch fuller and coming  into the right-hander who flicks it to mid-wicket and takes a single.
On a good length outside off and nicely blocked by Chandimal.
The batsman has driven it through mid on for nothing.
FOUR! Short and rising into the body of Chandimal, who swivels across to play the pull. He gets enough on the ball and plays it fine to the boundary behind the keeper.
Played to the point region by the batsman to end a successful over for Shannon.
On a driveable length and Danajaya complies but fails to make a contact.
Akila Dananjaya strides out to bat.

OUT! This has been the trend of this Sri Lankan innings. Gabriel has another with the same probing delivery. He keeps it around off, on a back of a length and makes the left-hander have a go at it. Dickwella's feet go nowhere as he pokes at the delivery and Shai Hope takes a good forward diving catch at gully. Another one bites the dust.
Touch short and the batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On a good length outside off and left alone by the batsman.
Dickwella defends it from within the crease.
Leaves the wider delivery for the keeper.
Probing line and length from Holder. He is mixing up his pace pretty well. Dinesh is adamant on blocking it.
Back of a length outside off and punched to the fielder at covers for nothing.
Nicely behind again. Touch fuller and defended with authority by the Sri Lankan skipper.
Similar length and into the stumps. Dinesh blocks it off the front foot.
On a good length and seaming away off the pitch. Holder is getting the old ball to swing and is keeping the batsman guessing.
Jason Holder to continue.
Flicked off his pads for nothing.
Touch short and punched away through the covers for another single.
Angled into the ribs and tucked away to backward square leg. Bishoo stationed there makes a good stop.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
FOUR! Short, directed into the ribs of the batsman. The ball gets extra bounce from the pitch and flies off the top edge to the boundary behind the keeper. Welcome runs for Dickwella.
On a good length outside off, Dinesh punches it in the cover region and changes the strike.
Full and on the pads, Dickwella flicks it in the air to the vacant mid-wicket region and takes two.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot to mid-wicket. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Bouncer from Holder but its too high. The umpire signals a wide.
FOUR! Easy runs for the set batsman. Touch too straight and into the body, Chandimal swivels and gets it fine behind for a boundary.
Short, wide outside off, swinging away and flying off the pitch. Chandimal went across for the pull but failed to make contact. A diving stop by the Windies keeper.
Gets closer to the batsman this time and blocked with the full face of the bat.
Probing line from Holder. Back of a length, outside off and making Chandimal play at it.
Short of a length, on his hips and flicked uppishly to deep square leg for an easy two.
Touch fuller this time and punched to mid off.
Gets behind the line of the back of the length delivery and defends it off the back foot.
Played to mid-wicket by the batsman for nothing.
Back of a length and seaming away after pitching. Dickwella gets his right leg away to make some room, swings the willow but misses.
That one flew off the length but it is outside the leg stump and no danger to the batsman.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Full and outside off, punched from the front foot through the covers and a run taken.
Drives the full ball from his crease straight to mid off.
Dickwella has played it to the point region from his crease.
Back of a length and again into the ribs. Chandimal gets it away to the vacant square leg region. One run added to the total and brings 1000 runs for him as a skipper.
On a good length, outside off and stays touch low. The batsman manages to get it to the short cover fielder.
Jason Holder to share the ball from the other end.
Gets behind the line and blocks the short of a length delivery.
Touch too straight and on the hips of Chandimal. He dabs it fine and takes a single.
Flicks it off his hips and takes a single from the leg side.
Similar length and into the body. Dickwella tries to make room by moving away from the stumps and manages to chop it to the fielder at gully. Risky from the Sri Lankan keeper.
Wide of the crease and angling it away from the left-hander who pokes at the shortish delivery but fails to make contact.
Starts with an angled in delivery and Chandimal guides it behind to change strike.
Players make their way out to the middle for the last session of the day. Dinesh Chandimal is on strike and Miguel Cummins will bowl the first over post Tea.
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

Windies won't be too disappointed either. Shannon Gabriel has been probing since morning and he has picked up a wicket in this session as well while Kemar Roach and Devendra Bishoo have kept things tight. They will be hoping to get the big wicket of Dinesh Chandimal and then clean up the tail as soon as possible. Last session of the day promises to be action-packed. Catch us on the other side of the break.

End of another absorbing session. The Windies still hold the upper hand but this has been a much better passage of play for Sri Lanka. They have their skipper to thank for who has provided some stability to the fragile middle order after the dismissal of Kusal Perera. He found good support from Kusal Mendis but the youngster failed to deliver in a substantial manner. He kept going to conjure up his 17th Test fifty and is looking settled to play a big innings. He has lost partners at the other end but he has been the epitome of calmness.
A lot of air on this one as well, Dickwella defends it solidly. THAT SHALL BE TEA ON DAY 1!
Slow through the air, defended from within the crease.

A bit of miscommunication but safe! Quick and short on middle, Dickwella makes room and cuts it towards extra cover. Calls for the single initially but realizes that it is not on. He is quick to send his partner back.
Slow through the air outside off, defended off the front foot.
On a flatter trajectory, kept out from within the crease.
Flighted ball on off, driven towards wide mid on for a single.
Tossed up outside off, pushed to covers off the front foot.
The batsman has driven that ball straight back.

This time the shot selection is not good. On a shorter length around off, Niroshan again goes for the paddle sweep but this time he misses. He is struck on the pads but it is probably outside the line. Hence, no appeal from the hosts.
A bit cheeky but effective! Down the leg side, good shot selection from Dickwella as he paddle sweeps it to fine leg for a couple.
Slow through the air on middle and off, Niroshan lunges forward in defense.
Tossed up delivery around off, kept out watchfully.
Roston Chase has been called into the attack. The batsmen need to be alert as the passage before a break can prove to be dangerous.
Shorter in length, punched off the back foot to the off side.
Well bowled! Floated generously on off. It dips in late and spins away sharply. Chandimal takes a stride forward, watches it closely and makes a good leave.
Fuller in length on middle, Chandimal lunges forward in defense.
Dickwella comes back to the flatter delivery and punches it to deepish mid on for a single.
Floated delivery, defended solidly off the front foot.
Hangs back to the shortish delivery and blocks it with a straight bat.
Back of a length ball outside off, Chandimal rises with the bounce and blocks it nicely.
On a good length outside off, shaping in. Dinesh covers the line and makes an assured leave.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Short of a length ball around the hips, tucked around the corner for a run.

Flashy and reckless! Don't think the situation calls in to play such a stroke. Length ball outside off, Dickwella tries to force it through the line but gets beaten. Luck has favoured him till now but he can run out of it as well.
There is a surprise element that Roach has always got up his sleeve. He runs in effortlessly and bowls a yorker outside off. Dickwella does well to block it.
Tossed up generously outside off, Chandimal drives it crisply but finds the man at covers.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Bishoo continues to bowl it full and Chandimal pushes it back to him.
Fuller ball on off, defended stoutly off the front foot.
Slow through the air outside off, Dinesh lets it go.
Flatter in trajectory, kept out watchfully.
Outside off, left alone.

This is the fourth occasion in this over that he has been foxed. Good length ball wide outside off, Dickwella with minimal foot movement tries to drive it on the up. He is nowhere close to the ball and the bowler once again gets a moral advantage.
In the channel outside off, this time sanity prevails for the Sri Lankan wicket-keeper and he leaves it alone.
Peach! Angling in with the arm but seaming away after hitting the deck to catch Dickwella off guard and go past his outside edge.
A play and a miss again! On a length outside off, Niroshan tries to lift it over covers but only connects with thin air. He needs to be careful.
Rash from Dickwella! Shortish ball outside off and there is a bit of room on offer. Still it is not much to go for an expansive stroke. Dickwella flashes at it but misses.
Comes well forward to a loopy ball and defends it with authority.
Very full on middle, Chandimal clears his front leg and jams it out.
Makes the batsman play this time but he is solid as a rock.
Straighter one well outside off, left alone.
Bishoo drags his length back. Dinesh spots it and gets behind it with ease.
Quicker through the air around off, patted back towards the bowler.
Stump-to-stump line, Dickwella shuffles a touch and pats it back to the bowler.
Bumper from Roach, Dickwella ducks under it.
In two minds! Back of a length outside off. Niroshan shapes to leave it but defends it to the off side.
Fullish delivery, driven convincingly to covers this time.

Tentative! On a length around off, holds a bit in the pitch. Dickwella comes half-forward in order to defend it but the ball hits the higher part of his bat. The ball lobs towards the cover region but falls short of the fielder.
Well bowled! Roach runs in from around the wicket and bowls a good length ball. It is coming in initially but moves away eventually. Dickwella keeps his bat inside the line to leave it alone.
Kemar Roach returns for a burst.
Tossed up ball on middle, Dinesh clears his front leg and pushes it to mid on.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Spinning down the leg side, tucked through mid-wicket for a brace.
Fullish delivery on off, driven crisply to Bishoo.
Chandimal uses his feet to this one and blocks it out.
Floated around off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Shortish ball outside off, Dickwella lets it go.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Overpitched outside off, eased through covers to get off the mark with a brace.
Back of a length ball, defended with a straight bat.
In the zone outside off, left alone.
Niroshan Dickwella comes out to bat.

OUT! Roshen Silva's struggle continues! The man who was terrific upfront has produced another peach to hand his side another breakthrough. There is enough in the track to keep the bowlers interested and the hosts have bowled with a lot of discipline. Gabriel steams in hard and bowls an effort ball in the corridor of uncertainty. It takes off after pitching and climbs on Silva. He hops but is in an awkward position to counter it. Tries to fend it eventually but the ball takes the splice of the bat and flies towards the slip cordon. Jason Holder at third slip is sharp as a hawk and takes a good catch.
Fuller in length, driven crisply towards Bishoo who does well to get low and stops a few runs for his side.
Slips in a googly outside off. Chandimal reads it well and defends it solidly.
Straighter one from Bishoo on off, pushed confidently off the front foot to mid off.
Tossed up ball in line of the stumps, Chandimal lunges forward in defense.
Similar ball, cut square of the wicket on the off side.
Starts off his new spell with a shortish ball. Dinesh hangs back and cuts it towards point.
Devendra Bishoo returns for a bowl.
Once again wide outside off, Silva ignores it.
This one is on a full length but way, way outside off. Roshen Silva watches it sail through to the keeper.
Pacy delivery well outside off, Roshen lets it be.
Goes deep in the crease to the back of a length ball and defends it stoutly.
Good length ball in line of the stumps, Roshen takes his bottom hand off the handle of the bat and defends it watchfully.
The batsman works it down the leg side.

17th Test fifty for Dinesh Chandimal! This is only the third 50-plus score by a Sri Lankan skipper in West Indies. He has been resolute on a tough surface and has got the reward as well. Back of a length ball on middle and leg, Chandimal works it away through backward square leg and comes back for a brace. The Sri Lankan skipper was dropped on 14 by Devon Smith and has made the most of it. Needs to convert this into a big one.
Hangs back to the length delivery and blocks it with a straight bat.
Pitched right up on off, pushed off the front foot to extra cover.
Nicely bowled and equally well played! Late swing on that one, moving away from Chandimal. He covers the line and blocks it to the off side.
Good length ball outside off, Chandimal knows where his off stump is and makes a good leave.
Fractionally overpitched outside off, driven crisply but straight to the fielder at covers.
Well played! Full length ball on the pads, Chandimal tucks it with good timing through mid-wicket. The fielder chases it and saves a run for his side.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Nervy moments for the Sri Lankan skipper! Tries to cut a rising ball but once again is not in control. Thankfully for him, it falls in front of the point fielder.
Fuller in length, shaping in. Dinesh tries to block it but gets it off the inner half of the bat beside the pitch on the leg side.
Short of a length ball aimed towards the body, helped towards backward square leg.
A bit uppish but safe! Short of a length ball, Chandimal goes for a cut but doesn't bother to keep it down. The fielder at backward point is interested for a while but it bounces well short of him.
Solid! Fullish delivery, shaping in nicely. Silva with his bat and pad close together blocks it stoutly.
Tentative! Swinging in from outside off, goes off the inner half of the bat towards square leg and a run is taken.
Seaming down the leg side, Chandimal fails to flick it. Some work for Dowrich and he does it well.
Wide outside off, Chandimal doesn't fiddle with it.
Fullish delivery in the tight off stump channel, shaping away. Silva plays it with soft hands to covers and takes an easy single.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region.
Time for Drinks.
In the corridor outside off, the Sri Lankan skipper lets it go.
Surprise delivery from Gabriel. Silva did well to stay alert. Yorker which dips in late, the batsman gets his bat down in time and jams it out towards backward square leg. A run taken.
Tailing in significantly, kept out watchfully towards short leg.

Ouch, that will hurt! It came in a long way. Back of a length outside off, seaming in prodigiously. Roshen Silva doesn't know it is coming and tries to drop his wrists. However, he is right flush on the chest.
With a short leg in position for Silva, the ploy is to bounce him out. As expected, it is a short ball but the direction is wayward. Down the leg side and the batsman ducks under it comfortably.
Swinging down the leg side, Dinesh flicks it through backward square leg to get off strike.
Gabriel returns for a bowl.
On a driveable length outside off, swinging away sharply. Silva doesn't flirt with danger.
Full length ball outside off, moving away. Silva plays the inside line of it and sees it through safely.
Fuller length ball, considerable amount of wobble in the air. Silva is squared up a touch but manages to block it safely towards covers.
Similar length ball, angling in, tucked with a closed bat face towards mid-wicket.
Back of a length ball outside off, Dinesh doesn't flirt with it.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
That took off like an aeroplane! Good length ball outside off, climbs up alarmingly to go past the edge of Silva's bat. Dowrich has to collect it with his fingers pointing upwards.
Well bowled! Shoots off from a back of a length and goes past the hanging bat of Roshen.
Erring in line, towards the pads, helped to the leg side for a run.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the  back foot.
FOUR! This is the second time he has played this shot and has got the desired result. Short and a lot of width on offer. Chandimal chases it and flashes it off the outer half over the gully region.
Around the hips this time, clipped around the corner for a couple.
FOUR! Streaky runs! Pitched up ball outside off, Silva goes for a booming drive but gets a thick outside edge past the slip cordon and through to the fence. A successful over for Holder ends.
On a length, shaping in, Silva tries to play it across but is hit on the thigh pad.
Pitched up outside off, Roshen pushes it with soft hands to the cover region.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Leg bye! Down the leg side again, Dinesh tries to work it away but misses. The ball kisses his thigh pad and rolls to the leg side. A run taken.
Roshen Silva is the new man in.

OUT! Holder strikes and he is absolutely pumped up! Well, another stand which promised but failed to deliver big. The Windies continue to chip away at the wickets and stay on top of the game. Shortish ball down the leg side, there is a bit of extra bounce on offer. Mendis gets deceived due to it and closes his bat face early. As a result, a top edge is induced and the ball skies towards backward square leg. Dowrich lines it up and runs towards it. Judges it nicely and takes it on the move. A decent knock from Mendis comes to an end. Lately, he was looking itchy and has succumbed.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
On a length around off, seaming away after pitching. Dinesh is opened up in his stance but does well to block it towards covers.
Outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Risky! Cummins had a plan in mind and that almost worked. Back of a length ball directed towards the rib-cage area of the batsman. He plays it awkwardly towards leg gully. Bishoo stationed there leaps to his right but the ball sails over him. Too close for comfort.
FOUR! Pretty safe shot eventually! Short and wide outside off. Chandimal throws his bat at it but the ball flies off the top edge over the slip cordon and the ball races to the fence.
Veering in towards the pads, flicked sensibly through mid-wicket for a couple.
Similar delivery outside off, not close enough to induce a shot from Mendis.
On a length around off, Mendis covers the line and pats it to mid on.
Some wobble this time! Fuller length ball outside off, shapes away after landing. Mendis chooses to leave it alone.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Back of a length ball around off, defended solidly off the back foot.
Rush of blood from Mendis! Poor, poor cricket for him. Needs to be patient. Wide outside off, he flashes at it but misses.
Holder returns for a bowl.
Back of a length outside off, Dinesh gets on top of the bounce and guides it towards gully.
Down the leg side, swiped away to fine leg for a single.
Good running! Short of a length outside off, Chandimal taps it towards covers and calls his partner through for a well-judged single.
A fourth slip comes in for Chandimal.
Mendis was surprised there! Good length ball on middle and leg, comes a bit slowly off the surface. Mendis adjusts and helps it down to fine leg for a single.
Fuller in length outside off, patted to covers to rotate strike.
Good length ball outside off, defended from within the crease.
Nicely controlled! Shortish ball in line of the stumps, Mendis rolls his wrists on it and pulls it through mid-wicket for a brace.

FOUR! This one is more authoritative! Slightly overpitched, angling in. Mendis with a lot of confidence strokes it over mid on for another boundary. That brings up the 50-run stand between the duo. Need to keep the runs coming.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Mendis takes the aerial route and succeeds! Perhaps, this is the way to disturb the rhythm of Roach. Fullish delivery, veering in. Mendis with a free flow of the bat lifts it over  wide mid on. Has got enough behind it and the ball rolls to the fence.
On a length outside off, jagging in. Mendis defends it with his bat and pad close together.
In the zone outside off, Kusal doesn't flirt with it.

A short leg would have taken that! The Windies need to keep attacking, there is so much on the surface. Shortish delivery, rising on Chandimal. He tries to fend that off but the ball hits his gloves and falls in the vacant short leg region.
Outside off, left alone.

That was really difficult to deal with! Short of a length outside off, shoots off after pitching. Chandimal tries to ride the bounce but is deceived completely. Does well to drops his wrists eventually and sees the ball sail past him.
On a length outside off, holding its line. Dinesh lets it be.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Back of a length outside off, not fiddled with.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. Another good over from Roach.

Bonus runs for Sri Lanka! Bad luck for the hosts. Chandimal taps this towards covers and sets off. The fielder aims for the bull's eye at the bowler's end but the throw deflects off Chandimal's body and runs through to the long on fence. There is nothing you can do about it.

A lot is happening at the moment. Testing times for the visitors. Coming in with the initial angle around off and leaves Chandimal at the last moment as he goes for a push through the line. However, he doesn't connect.
Takes off from a short of a length, Dinesh watches it closely and lets it be.
Similar ball outside off, Chandimal leaves it again.
Short of a length outside off, left alone.
Fourth play and a miss in the over! Wide outside off, a loose shot from Mendis as he fails to connect again.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
That was a jaffa! Too good to get the outside edge. Angling in around the off stump. Mendis has no option but to play at it but the ball shapes away at the last moment to leave Mendis bamboozled.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Similar ball outside off, Kusal is not learning from his mistakes. Chases it again and gets foxed.
A play and a miss! Short of a length ball outside off, moving away after landing. Mendis pokes at it and gets beaten.
Cuts him into two halves! Angling in substantially from outside off and goes past the inside edge of Chandimal's hanging bat.

A big, big misjudgment but no harm done! Back of a length outside off, Mendis taps it towards covers and takes off and Chandimal responds as well. The fielder picks it up and has a shy at the striker's end but misses. The skipper was not even in the frame.
Slightly overpitched this time, driven past Roach and the batsmen come back for a couple.
Driven towards the mid off region.
FOUR! Stylish! Full length ball on the pads, Mendis flick it over square leg and the ball races to the fence.
Full length ball, pushed off the front foot to mid on.

DROPPED and FOUR! That was a sitter, Smith will be kicking himself. Can prove to be a costly miss. Back of a length ball in the corridor of uncertainty. It straightens a bit after pitching. That is enough to induce an outside edge as Chandimal pokes at it. Devon Smith at first slip takes it casually. Tries to catch it with hard hands to his right but the ball bursts through and runs to the fence.
Fuller in length outside off, played with an angled blade past the gully fielder for a couple.
Beaten! Good stuff from Cummins. He runs in hard and bowls a back of a length outside off. Chandimal pokes at it but is deceived by the extra bounce.
Well played! Short of a length ball outside off, punched nicely behind point for a brace.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Starts with a full length ball delivery on the pads, Chandimal clips it with soft hands towards mid-wicket and comes back for the second.
Miguel Cummins to bowl from the other end.
On a length, shaping in, defended solidly off the back foot.

Edged but safe! Roach pitches this one on a fuller length outside off and gets the ball to swing away a touch. Mendis goes for a flamboyant drive but only manages an outside edge towards gully. The fielder takes it on the bounce.
Similar length ball outside off, punched off the back foot towards point.
Mendis hangs back to the good length ball and defends it stoutly off the back foot.
Bye! Angling in from wide of the crease. Chandimal lets it go. Dowrich behind the stumps fails to collect it cleanly. The batsmen steal a run.
Fuller length ball outside off, holding its line. Chandimal plants his front foot across to let it be.
We are back for the afternoon session. Dinesh Chandimal and Kusal Mendis will continue their innings. Kemar Roach to bowl first up after Lunch. Here we go...
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

Kusal Perera was struggling but continued to fight on and found an able ally in Kusal Mendis. They stitched a 44-run stand and the signs were promising but Roach came back and struck instantaneously in his second spell to get rid of the former. From Sri Lanka's perspective, it is really vital that the pair of Mendis and Chandimal contribute something substantial. While, the hosts will be aiming to continue the domination. Join us shortly for the afternoon session.

We have witnessed an intriguing session of Test cricket and the home side would be really pleased with how things have gone so far. After winning the toss and electing to bat, the Sri Lankan openers found out that it will be tough work for them on a spicy surface against some penetrative bowling. Shannon Gabriel found his mojo and picked up two quick wickets with the new cherry. The debutant, Udawatte failed to impress while de Silva wasn't able to deliver as well on his return to the side.

FOUR! Can we call that a drop? It would be too harsh on the Windies keeper on so many levels. The last ball before Lunch gives us a moment of excitement. The hosts look disappointed but as Michael Holder points out on air, Dowrich couldn't have jumped any higher. Coming to the delivery, it is on a back of a length, around off and Mendis tries to get some easy runs over the keeper's head with a ramp shot but doesn't play it cleanly. The ball flies off the upper edge and just over the jumping, outstretched Dowrich, who manages to get just his fingertips to it. In the end, the ball has enough legs on it to race to the boundary. The Windies will be the happier side going into LUNCH ON DAY 1.
Full and outside off and punched off the front foot by Chandimal. One run added to total.
Plants his foot down and blocks it with intent.
This one is down the leg side and the batsman leaves it alone.
Looks to get forward to meet the full length delivery outside off but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
On a back of length and tapped to point region for nothing.
Touch short outside off and the Sri Lanka skipper goes back in his crease and cuts it square for a single.
Almost too full and Chandimal almost yorked himself but manages to keep it out somehow.
Plants his foot down and plays the flighted delivery to mid off for nothing.
Touch flatter on off, the batsman blocks it to the off side off the back foot.
Floated on off, blocked from the full face of the bat.
Flighted delivery around off and Chandimal punches it off the back foot.
Time for some spin. Devendra Bishoo to roll his arm over now.
On a good length outside off and in the probing channel. Mendis was looking to leave it but doesn't get his bat away in time. The ball hits the under edge and goes to the slip fielder on the bounce.
Pitches it around off and Mendis presents the full face of the bat.

Naah! He has been doing well to not to go after the wide ones but here there is a lapse in his concentration. Gabriel serves one wide outside off and entices the batsman. He goes for the booming drive but fails to make a connection.
Blocks the length delivery from his crease.
Goes wide of the crease once again, on a good length and Chandimal flicks it off his pads to fine leg for a single.
Short of a length on middle and leg and hit straight to the short mid-wicket fielder.
Gets behind the line and blocks it down the pitch to end the over.
The batsman has driven it straight down the ground.

Another one sneaks in and this time past Mendis. Similar probing length on off stump and coming in after pitching. Mendis gets on the front foot to block it but the ball darts in and goes over the stumps.
Angled length delivery and worked on the leg side for a single.

Oh my my! Chandimal has no idea how and where the ball is jagging in from. Roach goes over the wicket to the new batsman, lands it on a good length and angles it into the stumps. The ball pitches and seams into the batsman and sneaks between the pad and bat and even misses the stumps. Roach is making life difficult for the Sri Lankan batsmen.
Chandimal chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

FOUR! Beautifully done this by Mendis. Easy peasy for him. Gabriel goes wide of his crease, keeps it on a short of a length and targets his ribs. The batsman gets inside the line of the delivery and tickles it to the fine leg fence for the second boundary of the over.
Played to point from the back foot for nothing.
FOUR! And just like that, Mendis decides to go after the full delivery on off. Gets his foot down the pitch and hits it fiercely down the ground. Mendis too getting a move on now.
Touch short and coming into the batsman, who taps it to point and runs a quick single.
Touch too straight on the pads, the batsman tickles it through backward square leg. The fielder at fine leg runs to his left and stops the batsmen to two.
Wide outside and left alone by Chandimal.
Shannon Gabriel is back on.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
On a good length outside off and a square drive from Mendis but couldn't get it past the fielder there.
Almost another one for Roach. What a spell of bowling from the fast bowler. Hitting the good length and forces the drive from Mendis, who fails to make contact.
Works the shortish delivery to backward square leg and gets off the mark with a single.
Wide outside off stump, Chandimal leaves it alone.
The Sri Lankan captain, Dinesh Chandimal strides out to bat. A lot of responsibility lies on his shoulders to guide his side to safe harbors.

OUT! Finally! Roach finally has his man. He constantly troubled the opener in his first spell and has struck with immediate effect in his second one. Bowling it in the probing off stump channel has paid dividends. Lands the ball on a short of a length, angles it in and extracts extra bounce off the pitch. Perera is caught in the crease as he fends at it and ends up getting it from the splice of the bat behind. The Windies skipper, Jason Holder is safe as a house at third slip and Kemar Roach rejoices his 150th Test wicket. The dangerous looking Perera is walking back. The promising 44-run stand comes to an end. Sri Lanka continue to lose wickets at regular intervals.
Kemar Roach is back for a bowl.
Outside off and the batsman ignores it.
Mendis lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Short of a length and played to the leg side for nothing.
Goes around the wicket, angles it into the left-hander and troubles him. Perera gets an under edge and the ball rolls wide of the keeper. One run taken.
Wide and left alone by the batsman.
Short and wide again, Perera flashes his bat again and the ball lobs in the air for a while. The fielder from backward point runs to his left and throws the ball back. Two runs added to the total.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Touch too short and into the body of the batsman, hits him on the thigh pad.
Mendis defends it from within the crease.
Play and a miss. A touch short outside off and takes extra bounce. The batsman goes for the cut but misses.
Cummins goes full around off and nicely defended by the batsman off the front foot.
Rides the extra bounce outside off stump and dabs it to gully.
Kusal Perera lets the ball go outside his off stump.

Jason is getting something out of this pitch. On a good length just outside off, Perera tries to punch it but the ball goes from the inside edge of the bat. They take two from the vacant mid-wicket region.
Lets the good length delivery pass to the keeper.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
OOH! Almost chopped on. On a short of a length, angling away from the batsman. He goes for the cut but gets a thick inside edge and the ball almost hits his stumps. Close but not close enough.

FOUR! Anything short and wide has been punished by Perera. He gets another one outside off and he carves it through the point-cover region for a boundary. Four boundaries in the last seven deliveries for the left-hander.
Back of a length ball on middle and off, the right-hander rises with the bounce and blocks it right under his eyes.
Almost a replica of the previous delivery as Mendis doesn't fiddle with it.
This one stays low! Fuller length ball outside off, left alone.

This is good stuff from Cummins! Continues to bowl it in the tight off stump line and the ball straightens a touch after landing. Kusal is opened up in his stance but does well to defend it towards point.
In the corridor of uncertainty, no real movement on this occasion. Kusal Mendis plants his front foot across to let it through.
Short of a length delivery, angling in, Mendis camps back and blocks it nicely.
Bumper to end the over from Holder and Perera is happy to duck under it.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
And misses the very next ball after hitting last three for boundaries. Short of a good length and angling away from the left-hander who tries to get behind the line but misses.

FOUR! Bang! Hat-trick of boundaries. This is more of a slap than an off drive. Holder goes full outside off and Perera swings his bat from his crease and plays a short arm jab down the long off fence. The power in the shot almost took the non-striker out. Time for some fireworks!

FOUR! Creamed through covers. He surely has his eye in now. Gets a short of a length delivery outside off and makes full use of it. He gets forward and punches the ball through covers. Class written all over that shot.

FOUR! Nice and easy this. On a good length, angling into the hips and Perera pulls it nonchalantly through square leg for a boundary. He looks much better at the crease now than he was some 30 minutes back.
A touch too short this time angling into the left-hander, who rocks onto the back foot and punches it through covers for a couple.
Touch short but still too wide to make Mendis take notice of it. Another leave outside off.
Copy paste stuff from the bowler and the batsman.
Wide outside off and another leave by the batsman for the keeper.
Mendis shoulders arms to let that one through.
On a good length, outside off, left alone by the batsman.

Time for Drinks. The initial stage of play has belonged to the hosts. The bowlers have run in with intent on a green surface, landing the ball in good channels. Results have also come their way. It is a re-building phase for the visitors. Mendis and Perera need to grind it out and show the way to their side.
Nips in from a length and hits the batsman on his thigh pad. Extra bounce once again.
Gets behind the line and defends the good length delivery to point.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.

In the air... but safe! Short, wide and too high but the batsman wants to play at it. He goes after it and gets an edge. The ball goes high in the air, behind point and Devendra Bishoo runs after it but doesn't get even his hands to it. Difficult chance this and two runs are taken by the batsmen.
FOUR! Not shying away from the challenge is Kusal Perera. Short and touch too wide, Perera gets on his toes and cuts it through cover-point for a boundary. It will give him some confidence.
And... just short of the point fielder. Good length delivery, in the probing zone outside off and taking the edge but doesn't reach the fielder.
Short and outside off, and almost squares him up. The batsman does well to keep it down.

Again in two minds. To play or not to play. On a good length, outside off, Mendis gets his bat closer to the delivery but chooses to leave it at the last moment. Before he could pull out, the ball took the under edge towards the slip cordon.
Another short delivery. Mendis was looking to pull but chooses against the option and leaves it for the keeper.
Gets behind the angled delivery and blocks it from the crease.
Mendis chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Works the short of length delivery to the leg side and scampers for two.
Short and into the rib-cage, the batsman pulls and gets it over the infield. The ball hangs in the air and thuds into the wet outfield at deep mid-wicket. Two more runs taken.
Fuller and on the off stump, Kusal gets behind the line and plays it with soft hands. The ball lands in front of the gully fielder. Good calm batting from the left-hander.
On a short of a length and flicked off his pads to square leg. Another run added to the total.
Taps to cover region and takes a single to change the strike.

Close shave! Attempted pull on the short delivery but the connection isn't right as it hits high on his bat. The batsmen take off and the fielder at short mid-wicket runs to his right and throws the ball back quickly to the non-striker's end. Had it hit, it could have been close.
On a good length outside off, Mendis defends it to the covers for nothing.
The skipper, Jason Holder comes in for a burst.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

Was that a catch? No. Cummins arches his back and extracts some bounce. Perera jumps to get behind the line but misses it. It hits him on his chest and lobs in the air and lands just in front of the diving slip fielder.
This one is down the leg side and the batsman leaves it alone.
On a fullish length into the pads, Kusal Perera flicks it but can't get it past Devendra Bishoo at square leg.
Bumper from Cummins and the batsman ducks under it.
Awkward bounce again. The ball lands on a back of a length and jumps into the ribs of Perera. He does well to get bat on it while his hand came off the handle.
Miguel Cummins is into the attack.
Mistimes the off drive off the front foot and hits it straight to the fielder.
Bowled at 144.0 kph and the batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
FOUR! Welcome runs for the visitors. Gets some width from Gabriel on a good length and the batsman slashes hard and cuts it through to the backward gully region for a boundary.
Short and into the body of the batsman, who tries to poke at it but doesn't get any bat on it.
Kusal gets up on his toes to play that one.

OOH! That extra bounce. Gabriel is making the Sri Lankan batsmen dance on this green pitch. The ball pitches on a back of a length and gets the extra bounce off the pitch. Mendis gets behind the line to defend it. The bounce troubles him a bit, hits him on the splice of the bat and the ball lands just in front of the short leg fielder stationed there.
Lets the last ball of the over through to the keeper.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Another swing and another miss. Perera has been on some potion of sorts. He has not edged even one till now. Similar delivery from Roach, on a good length and outside off but still no edge.
Too wide to entice the batsman for a shot.
Wide down the leg side, no trouble at all for the batsman.
Angles it a bit too much and the ball goes down the leg side. Good length but misses the line.
FOUR! Off the mark in style! Some room on a good length for Mendis to free his arms and he obliges with a fierce cut. The ball goes to the right of the fielder at gully and rushes to the boundary.
Mendis shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Kusal Mendis comes out to bat. He scored a brilliant century in the previous game and was the lone warrior for his side. Can he come to the fore again?

OUT! Gabriel has another and Sri Lanka lose their second. Fiery stuff from the fast bowler. He goes wide of the crease and bowls it on a back of a length. The ball seams in substantially after landing and catches the batsman by surprise. De Silva tries to cover the line but fails to counter it. The ball hits his right elbow and ricochets onto the stumps. He looks in a lot of pain, holding his arm and the physio comes rushing in to check. Hopefully, it won't be a major injury as he is a very important member of the team. The visitors are in some early trouble.
De Silva defends it from within the crease.
FOUR! Up and over from De Silva! Short and a lot of width, the batsman has no intention of keeping it down and hits it over to the third man region for a boundary.
Short of a good length outside off, the batsman punches it off his toes through cover-point. Two runs added to the total.
Kusal shoulders arms to let that one through.
That similar old story. Perera and the delivery outside off stump. But credit to him for holding his line. The ball passes the outside edge once again.
The ball is too wide on the off side for the batsman to make any contact.
WIDE! Goes too wide and outside the tramline of off stump. The umpire stretches his arms and signals a wide.

Finally gets one from the bat. Short of a length, coming into the left-hander and he connects with his bat but touch late. The ball roll to the deep mid-wicket region from the inside half of the bat and the batsmen take two.

And again! I have lost count now. I don't know how many times he has tried to get behind the line of the angled in delivery and missed. Roach gets fuller, just outside off stump. Perera pushes at it but gets beaten all ends up. He is yet to get off the mark.
Touch too straight and down the leg side. He has been consistent till now with his line and length. But misses his mark this time. Perera gets his hands away from the delivery.
On a good length, wide outside off, and ignored by the batsman.
Gabriel goes wide of the crease, pitches it on a fuller length and angles it into the pads. The batsman blocks it in front of his eyes.
No interest in fetching the wide ones. Let's one through again.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Gets behind the good length delivery and defends it off the front foot.
De Silva lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Roach is resolute. Not letting him off the hook. And Perera is struggling big time. Another play and a miss outside off.
No, it isn't happening. Goes fetching a wide one and misses again.
On a short of a good length and outside off stump, Perera lets one through.
Another play and a miss! Almost identical to the previous one.

And.... misses again! How is this happening? Perera has tried to get behind these angled in deliveries almost every single time and yet, he has missed 99 percent of them. Some appeal from the keeper but the bowler isn't interested.
WOW! Lethal stuff from the lanky pacer. Keeps the batsman on his toes, and brings it in with the angle. Perera plays inside the line of the short of the length delivery and gets beaten.
Similar shot but this time in the gap. Takes a couple as the ball goes to the sweeper cover region.
Cover drive off the length ball straight to the fielder.

FOUR! Carved nicely! Short of a length and climbing up to the right-hander. De Silva stays tall and pulls the ball square of the wicket. One hand comes off the handle but still has enough to reach the square leg boundary. De Silva is fighting fire with fire!
Defended the short of a length delivery from the crease.
Dhananjaya de Silva comes in at No. 3. He is back in the side and will be eager to impress.

OUT! Gone! Ideal start for the Windies and the players are ecstatic. That channel of uncertainty, I tell you! Keeps it on a back of a length, angling in and straightening after pitching. Udawatte has no option other than getting his bat in line. The ball moves away a touch and kisses the outside edge on the way. The Windies skipper, Jason Holder at third slip takes a nice diving catch to his right. Gabriel has tasted early blood. Disappointment for the debutant, not the way he would have wanted to begin his Test career.
Gabriel goes around the wicket straightaway to Udawatte, on a short of a length and almost squaring up the debutant. He manages to defend it somehow off the back foot.
Shannon Gabriel to share the new ball from the other end. Three slips and a gully in place for him as well.
And finally lets one go outside the off stump to end the over. Short of a good length and outside off, Perera doesn't fiddle with it.
Another play and a miss. On a similar length and wide of off stump, Kusal goes for a loose drive and gets foxed.
Goes chasing the wide one and fails to make contact. Nice enticing bowling from Roach.

Peach of a delivery from Roach! Absolute killer! That missed everything. Roach puts the ball on a good length, angling into the batsman and straightens after pitching. Perera plays down the wrong line and fails to make contact. The ball misses the outside edge and the off stump as well. Close call!
On a similar length and wide of the reach of Perera, who swings his bat like a golf stick and misses the ball.
Straightaway on a length, into the left-hander and angling away. Nicely defended by the batsman.

We are finally set to get underway. It is a gloomy morning with no signs of any sunshine around. Kusal Perera and the debutant, Mahela Udawatte stride out to open the innings for Sri Lanka. Kemar Roach to begin the proceedings with the brand new cherry. He is one shy of 150 Test wickets. Three slips, a short leg and a gully in place. Here we go...

Jason Holder says that they are playing with the same team and he is happy with his side's performance. Feels that they need to stick to the basics which they executed really well in the previous game. Reckons there is a bit of grass on the surface and his bowlers would like to exploit that upfront.

Dinesh Chandimal says that they will bat first. Announces that there are four changes. Adds that Gamage got injured and Mathews has gone back home. States there are a few tactical changes as well - Rangana Herath and Dilruwan Perera have been dropped. Mentions that Mahela Udawatte and Kasun Rajitha are making their debuts. Ends by saying that they had a good team meeting and have made some good plans.
TOSS - Sri Lanka win the toss and opt to bat.

PITCH REPORT - Jeff Dujon assessing the surface says that there will be consistency in bounce and pace. Mentions that there is a lot of grass on it and a bit of moisture. Feels that Day 2 will be good for batting. Further adds that if you get in, you can bat long and make runs. Reckons there will be assistance for the pacers as there is a considerable amount of grass on the surface. Ends by saying that the toss is not that important and the commitment and skill levels are what matter.

Sri Lanka coach, Chandika Hathurusingha, says that the mood in the camp is good. States that the scores suggest that they lost by a big margin but they were closer than that. Mentions that the duke ball needs time to adjust to. Informs there are a lot of positives in their side. Credits the likes of Kumara and Lakmal for their probing bowling. States that it is a concern as they took a lot of time to dismiss the last five Windies batsmen. Informs that there are unfortunately a few forced changes but they are confident about their abilities. Ends by saying that they anticipated some injuries and that is why they traveled with 17 players.

Sri Lanka, on the other hand, were bland overall. The batsmen did not capitalize on the starts, the bowlers were good in patches but failed to be consistent while the catching was shoddy. The experienced campaigners, Dinesh Chandimal and Rangana Herath, need to take responsibility and guide their team. The morale is low at the moment but they are a really potent side. Expect them to put in their all. Promises to be a cracking contest!

Hello and a warm welcome to the coverage of the second Test between West Indies and Sri Lanka in St Lucia. The hosts are on a high after a brilliant performance in the previous game. They clicked as a unit and delivered on all fronts. The likes of Dowrich and Chase were in their elements and helped the cause of their side.
